title: SBCA Taps Industry Veteran to Steer Structural Building Components into a Tech-Driven Future
summary: The Structural Building Components Association (SBCA) has appointed seasoned executive Steve Skodak as its new Executive Director, effective September 10, 2026. Skodak's three decades of leadership experience are poised to guide the association and the broader industry through an era of rapid technological advancement and sustainability demands.
content:
BILLINGS, Mont. – The Structural Building Components Association (SBCA), a critical advocate for the engineered wood components industry, has announced the appointment of Steve Skodak, CAE, CFRE, as its new Executive Director. The move, effective September 10, 2026, signals a strategic pivot as the association looks to navigate the increasingly complex intersection of construction, technology, and environmental responsibility.

Skodak brings a formidable resume, boasting over 30 years of leadership experience within various professional associations. His background isn't just about management; it’s about steering organizations through periods of significant change and fostering collaboration across diverse stakeholder groups. For an industry at the cusp of widespread digital transformation—from advanced manufacturing techniques and AI-driven design to sustainable material innovation—Skodak’s proven ability to champion growth and adapt to evolving landscapes will be invaluable.

His leadership comes at a crucial juncture for structural building components. With global demand for efficient, sustainable construction on the rise, and mounting pressures to innovate amidst labor shortages and supply chain complexities, the SBCA’s role as a standard-setter and thought leader is more important than ever. Skodak's vision is expected to emphasize the integration of cutting-edge technologies, further advocating for prefabrication, modular construction, and the intelligent use of engineered wood products to build a more resilient and tech-forward future.

This appointment isn’t merely a change in personnel; it represents a commitment by the SBCA to embrace the future of building science. Under Skodak’s guidance, the association is poised to accelerate the adoption of smarter building practices, driving both economic efficiency and environmental stewardship across the entire construction ecosystem.
keyTakeaways: Steve Skodak has been appointed as the new Executive Director of the Structural Building Components Association (SBCA).
Skodak brings over 30 years of leadership experience, expected to drive strategic growth and adaptation within the industry.
His leadership is anticipated to accelerate technological adoption, sustainable practices, and innovative construction methods in structural building components.
